pandals.name: Debibari Boro Debi Puja
pandals.committee_name: Debibari Durga Puja Committee / Koch Royal Trust
pandals.address: Debi Bari Road, Cooch Behar Bazar, Cooch Behar 736101
pandals.google_maps_query: Debibari Durga Mata Mandir Cooch Behar West Bengal
pandals.description: The Boro Debi Puja at Debibari Temple is the most significant heritage Durga Puja in Cooch Behar district, observed for over 500 years. Initiated by the Koch dynasty, this puja is fundamentally different from conventional Durga Puja. The idol does not feature the traditional children (Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik, Ganesha) — instead, the Goddess is flanked by Jaya and Vijaya. The idol is crafted from Maina wood by the same Chitrakar family for generations. The blood-red Goddess rides a lion/leopard. Ceremonial cannon fire during Mahashtami historically signalled the start of rituals for all other pujas in the town. Tantric traditions including Gupta Puja on Ashtami night are preserved.
pandals.historical_significance: Over 500 years old. Oldest Durga Puja in Cooch Behar region. Founded during Koch dynasty era (Maharaja Biswasingha or Maharaja Narnarayan). The Debibari is the seat of the Koch royal family's Kuladevi. Unique non-immersed Maina wood idol tradition predates modern Sarbojanin puja culture.
pandals.cultural_significance: Represents the fusion of indigenous Koch, Tantric, and Brahmanical traditions. The cannon fire tradition, the unique Jaya-Vijaya iconography, and the Maina wood craftsmanship are irreplaceable cultural heritage of North Bengal.
known_for: Jaya & Vijaya instead of traditional children
pandals.notes: This is the single most historically important Durga Puja in the entire Cooch Behar district. The Debibari temple complex is separate from the Cooch Behar Palace (Rajbari).

pandals.description: One of the most iconic and oldest clubs in Cooch Behar, Rocky Club is a landmark community Durga Puja known throughout the district for its innovative, thought-provoking themes. Past themes like 'Protha' (tradition) have received widespread appreciation. Located on the main Raj Rajendra Narayan Road, it is a must-visit during pandal hopping.
pandals.historical_significance: One of the oldest clubs in Cooch Behar. Long tradition of theme-based creative pandals.
pandals.cultural_significance: Sets the cultural tone for the Durga Puja season in Cooch Behar. Known for balancing modern creativity with respect for tradition.
pandals.notes: Consistently ranked among the top pandals in Cooch Behar district.

pandals.name: Madan Mohan Temple Durga Puja
pandals.google_maps_query: Madan Mohan Temple Cooch Behar West Bengal
pandals.description: The Madan Mohan Temple, constructed by Maharaja Nripendra Narayan (1885–1889), is the spiritual center of Cooch Behar's Vaishnava culture. While primarily a Krishna temple housing the Koch royal kuladevata, it hosts Durga Puja-related ceremonies and is a focal point for the festive season. The temple complex also houses Ma Kali, Ma Tara, and Ma Bhavani deities.
pandals.historical_significance: Built by Maharaja Nripendra Narayan. Koch royal kuladevata temple. Houses Lord Madan Mohan alongside multiple goddesses. Famous for annual Raas Mela.
pandals.cultural_significance: Spiritual and cultural center of Cooch Behar. Annual Raas Mela is one of the largest festivals in North Bengal.
pandals.notes: Primarily a Vaishnava temple but integral to Durga Puja season in Cooch Behar.

pandals.name: Baneswar Shiva Temple Durga Puja
pandals.address: Baneswar, 10 km north of Cooch Behar town, Cooch Behar
pandals.google_maps_query: Baneswar Shiva Temple Cooch Behar West Bengal
pandals.year_started: Ancient (legends date to 1100 BCE; renovated 17th century)
pandals.description: The Baneswar Shiva Temple, located about 10 km north of Cooch Behar town, is one of the most ancient temple sites in the district. The temple is believed to date back to 1100 BCE with associations to Raja Banasura. The structure was renovated by Maharaja Pran Narayan of the Koch dynasty in the 17th century. The sanctum is located below plinth level. A sacred pond with black softshell turtles adds to the site's unique character. Durga Puja celebrations at this temple-adjacent site carry deep historical and spiritual significance.
pandals.historical_significance: One of the oldest temple sites in Cooch Behar. Legends dating to 1100 BCE. Koch dynasty renovation in 17th century. State-protected monument.
pandals.cultural_significance: Sacred pilgrimage site. Unique below-ground sanctum. Sacred turtles.
pandals.notes: Primarily a Shiva temple. Durga Puja celebrations at this site require further verification of current scope.

recommended_supabase_schema.relationships: A pandal belongs to one district, one subdivision, one block. It may optionally belong to a gram_panchayat and/or locality. A pandal has many categories (one primary), many tags, many sources, and many year-records. Clusters contain many pandals (many-to-many via cluster_pandals).
